record.original_question: Asymptotically evaluate each of the following additive-divisor correlations: sum_{n<=x} d3(n) d3(n+1); sum_{n<=x} d(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); for every kappa in (0,1), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d(n+1) d(n+2); and for every kappa in (2,3), sum_{n<=x} d_kappa(n) d3(n+1).

evidence.quote: Problems on additive divisor sums: Asymptotically evaluate sum d3 (n)d3 (n + 1). Asymptotically evaluate sum d(n)d(n + 1)d(n + 2). Let κ in (0, 1). Asymptotically evaluate sum dκ (n)d(n + 1)d(n + 2). Let κ in (2, 3). Asymptotically evaluate sum dκ (n)d3 (n + 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$ and an integer $k\ge 2$, let
$$d_k(n)=\#\{(a_1,\dots,a_k)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^k : a_1a_2\cdots a_k=n\},$$
so that $d(n)=d_2(n)$ is the usual divisor function and $d_3(n)$ is the ternary divisor function. For a real number $\kappa>0$, define the generalized divisor function $d_\kappa(n)$ as the $n$-th Dirichlet coefficient of $\zeta(s)^\kappa$, i.e. via the Dirichlet series
$$\zeta(s)^{\kappa}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{d_\kappa(n)}{n^s}\qquad(\Re s>1),$$
so that $d_\kappa$ is multiplicative with $d_\kappa(p^a)=\binom{\kappa+a-1}{a}$ for primes $p$ and $a\ge 0$.

Establish asymptotic formulas, as $x\to\infty$, for each of the following shifted convolution (additive divisor) sums:

(a) $\displaystyle\sum_{n\le x} d_3(n)\,d_3(n+1)$;

(b) $\displaystyle\sum_{n\le x} d(n)\,d(n+1)\,d(n+2)$;

(c) for every fixed $\kappa\in(0,1)$, $\displaystyle\sum_{n\le x} d_\kappa(n)\,d(n+1)\,d(n+2)$;

(d) for every fixed $\kappa\in(2,3)$, $\displaystyle\sum_{n\le x} d_\kappa(n)\,d_3(n+1)$.

In each case, identify the main term explicitly and obtain a power-saving error term.
artifact.status_search_result: Asymptotic evaluation of additive divisor sums $\sum_{n\le x} d_k(n)d_\ell(n+h)$ is classical and known only when $\min(k,\ell)\le 2$. For $k=\ell=3$ (the ternary additive divisor problem) and the higher correlations listed, no asymptotic formula is known; this is widely cited as an open problem and is connected, via Conrey–Gonek and subsequent work, to the conjectural asymptotics of the sixth moment of the Riemann zeta-function. The generalized-divisor variants with non-integer $\kappa$ are likewise open.

status_evidence.title: The sixth moment of the Riemann zeta function and ternary additive divisor sums
status_evidence.snippet: A conjectural asymptotic formula for a family of ternary additive divisor sums is shown to imply an asymptotic formula for the sixth moment of zeta; the ternary additive divisor problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic formulas for sums of the form $\sum d_3(n)d_3(n+h)$ are conjectural and open.

status_evidence.title: Additive divisor problem - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic formulae for additive divisor sums remain elusive when both indices are at least 3.
status_evidence.claim: The general additive divisor problem with both divisor functions $d_k$, $d_\ell$ having $k,\ell\ge 3$ is unsolved.
